messages:
Maya (Ops): heads-up — finance flagged a ~3.2% token delta between the billing dashboard and invoices for AcmeCorp for the 2026-03-08..2026-03-14 window. found a spike in consumer lag on the metering ingest last friday. started a replay but it tripped rate limits and exited. creating thread to coordinate ledger-stitch + controlled backfill.
Ryan (oncall): :eyes: can you paste the replay job id and the error blob?
Maya (Ops): job id replay-42-1965100000. last few lines from the worker:
```
2026-03-12T02:13:47Z ERROR replay-worker: failed to push to event-router: 429 Too Many Requests - quota exceeded
replay-42-1965100000 aborted after 4 retries
```
Alex Chung: which stream/partitions were affected? offsets?
Maya (Ops): stream=metering-events-prod, partitions 3-7 mostly. consumer group=replay-stitch. commit lag on partition 5 hit ~156k messages. ingest metrics show sustained throttling from the router side.
IngestBot: Consumer lag: metering-events-prod partition=5 peak=156421 at 2026-03-12T02:14:05Z. Producer throttle_count increased +320 in 1h.
Neha Rao: likely root cause: replay traffic presented as normal client_id so router rate-limiter treated it like production traffic. replay bursts + concurrency exhausted the per-client burst window -> 429s. quick fix: make replay identify itself (job-id header) so router can apply a different burst policy / allowlist.
Sam Patel: from billing side — what does reconciliation look like? do we recompute token counts from raw events and stitch ledgers? how long will this take and will invoices change?
Alex Chung: propose runbook (short):
1) run a controlled replay for only partition 5 with dedupe + checksum enabled, low concurrency (4) and a replay header so router allowlists it. command:
```
./tools/replay --stream metering-events-prod --partition 5 --from-offset 120000 --to-offset 277000 \
  --job-id replay-42-1965100000 --dedupe --concurrency 4 --checksum
```
2) after successful replay, run ledger-stitch to recompute token counts for affected customers:
```
python scripts/reconcile_tokens.py --from 2026-03-08 --to 2026-03-14 --customers AcmeCorp --out reconciliation_acme_0314.csv
```
3) run automated invoice-delta job, compare to issued invoice, and surface any >0.5% delta to finance for manual review.
Ryan (oncall): i'll own execution. plan: start partition-5 controlled replay at 03:00 UTC tomorrow, validate checksums after completion, then kick reconcile script. will monitor router metrics and pause on first 429 spike.
Maya (Ops): action items:
- Ryan (oncall): run controlled replay + reconcile (ETA: 2026-03-13 06:00 UTC)
- Neha Rao: push router hotfix to accept a replay-job header and temp bump burst window for allowlisted jobs (PR #2345) — aim to ship before replay
- Alex Chung: prepare reconciliation CSV and verification checksums, smoke test locally
- Sam Patel: notify finance and prepare billing ticket template if invoice adjustments exceed threshold
- Maya (Ops): open customer support note for AcmeCorp and draft communication if invoice changes required
Sam Patel: please cc billing@redwood and create an internal customer escalation (support-12345) so finance has a ticket to reference.
Neha Rao: after replay + reconcile we'll ship the router patch to permanently treat replay traffic with a separate policy. PR link: https://git.redwood/infra/routers/pull/2345 — tests green in CI.
Alex Chung: sgtm. marking incident as P2, will record timestamps and ops timeline for post-incident RCA.
Maya (Ops): thanks — i'll update this thread with logs and the reconciliation CSV once done. if we see invoice delta >1% we'll escalate to leadership and notify Acme directly. :thumbsup:
